nodes.name: Electrodeposition of TM hydroxides
nodes.procedure: Transition metal (TM, Ni, Co, and Ni0.9Co0.1) hydroxide was electrodeposited on carbon cloth (working electrode, cathode) using Pt plate counter electrode and Hg/HgCl reference electrode. For Co(OH)2, 0.2 M Co(NO3)2 solution was used at current density of 10 mA cm^-2 for 600 s.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of TMOOH. We first prepared transition metal (TM, Ni, Co, and Ni0.9Co0.1) hydroxide via electrodeposition. For instance, to prepare Co(OH)2, the carbon cloth... Electrodeposition was carried out at a current density of 10 mA cm^-2 for 600 s.

nodes.name: Chemical oxidation to oxyhydroxide
nodes.procedure: The deposited Co(OH)2 was removed from carbon cloth and washed with deionized water several times. Then 0.1 g of Co(OH)2 and 30 ml of NaClO (5 wt%) solution were added to 50 ml Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave, pH adjusted to 13 with 0.1 M KOH solution. Heated to 100°C for 9 h to yield black CoOOH powder retrieved via centrifugation, washed with DI water 3 times, dried in vacuum oven. Other TMOOHs followed same procedure.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The autoclave was heated to 100°C, which was maintained for 9 h

nodes.name: Carbonate intercalation
nodes.procedure: Pristine TMOOH powder (0.1 g) was soaked in 0.1 M KOH solutions containing 0.01 M K2CO3, 0.05 M K2CO3, 0.10 M K2CO3 and 0.2 M K2CO3 respectively, for 12 h. The retrieved powder was washed with DI water at least three times and then dried in a vacuum drying oven. This produced TMOOH-xCO3^2- where x=1,2,3,4 corresponding to the four different K2CO3 concentrations.
nodes.source_text: Preparation of CO3^2--intercalated TMOOH. To obtain TMOOH-1CO3^2-, TMOOH-2CO3^2-, TMOOH·3CO3^2- and TMOOH-4CO3^2- model catalysts, pristine TMOOH powder (0.1 g) was soaked in 0.1 M KOH solutions with 0.01 M, 0.05 M, 0.10 M and 0.2 M K2CO3, respectively, for 12 h.

nodes.description: CO₃²⁻-looping (CL) test in 0.1 M KOH with varying carbonate concentrations
nodes.source_text: Figure 1b shows the relationship between the C O ₃ ²⁻ concentration (C_carb) and the OER overpotential at 10 mA cm⁻² (η₁₀). For NiCoOOH and CoOOH, essentially identical η₁₀ values are maintained in both the forward and back scans, yet a higher C_carb leads to a slight increase in η₁₀.

nodes.description: CO₃²⁻-looping (CL) test in 0.1 M KOH with varying carbonate concentrations

overpotential_at_10_mA/cm².value: decreases rapidly then stabilizes at 0.2 M

nodes.source_text: Conversely, the η₁₀ of NiOOH clearly negatively correlates with C_carb, which decreases rapidly in the region with a low C_carb and then slowly stabilizes when C_carb reaches 0.2 M. The maximum change in η₁₀ (Δη_m), which quantitatively shows the maximum impact on OER activity caused by the looping test, reaches 133 mV.

nodes.description: CO₃²⁻-CV-looping (CCL) test in 0.1 M KOH with varying carbonate concentrations
nodes.source_text: In the forward scan, C_carb has a much stronger influence on the η₁₀ values of CoOOH and NiCoOOH, where Δη_m exceeds 133 mV and 127 mV, respectively. In the backward scan, the change in η₁₀ becomes completely irreversible, resulting in prominent hysteresis loops for all catalysts. The value of Δη₁ is in the range of 118–125 mV.

nodes.description: OER LSV and MSLSV performance of TMOOH-xCO₃²⁻ model catalysts in 0.1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: Figure S17 compares the LSVs and Tafel slopes of various model catalysts... we also used differential electrochemical mass spectrometry (DEMS) to accurately determine the onset potential and Tafel slope from the MSLSVs... a higher degree of intercalation indeed worsens the OER performance of CoOOH and NiCoOOH. Compared with those of the pristine sample, the onset potential and Tafel slope of the most heavily intercalated sample increase by >100 mV and ~60 mV dec⁻¹, respectively.

the current density in all LSVs is normalized to the electrochemical surface area (ECSA), which does not vary significantly during both looping tests, as shown by the double-layer capacitance (C_dl) in Fig. S3.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns confirm successful and complete CO₃²⁻ intercalation in model catalysts as interplanar distance increases progressively from pristine samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns in Fig. S14 confirm successful and complete intercalation after the anion exchange process, as the corresponding interplanar distance increases progressively from that of the pristine samples to the most heavily intercalated samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pristine CoOOH (003) d-spacing is 0.419 nm, expands to 0.510 nm after CCL; NiCoOOH (006) from 0.360 nm to 0.376 nm; NiOOH (006) from 0.340 nm to 0.367 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed in Fig. 2d, the average interplanar spacings for pristine CoOOH (003), NiCoOOH (006), and NiOOH (006) are 0.419 nm, 0.360 nm, and 0.340 nm, respectively... After the CCL test, these d-spacings expand to 0.510 nm, 0.376 nm, and 0.367 nm, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mappings reveal carbon-rich shell ~4 nm thick on surface of spent catalysts after CCL test.
nodes.evidence_snippet: This speculation is further supported by elemental analysis via energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX, see Fig. S6), where the elemental mappings reveal that a carbon-rich shell with a thickness of ∼4 nm forms on the surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: C 1s XPS depth profile of spent CoOOH after CCL shows carbonate peak at ~289 eV disappearing at 5200 s etching (~5 nm); after CL at 1200 s (~1.1 nm). Surface carbonate concentrations for CoOOH series: 0%, 3.3%, 5.2%, 8.8%, 9.6%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2e shows the segments of C 1 s signals in CoOOH after the CCL test as a function of etching time. The carbonate peak, located at ~289 eV, weakens progressively with increasing depth. It completely disappears at 5200 s, which corresponds to a depth of ∼5 nm (see Fig. S1). Conversely, this carbonate peak of CoOOH after the CL test disappears much earlier at 1200 s.

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando SEIRAS shows peaks at 1500 cm⁻¹ (C–O) and 1680 cm⁻¹ (C=O) for interfacial CO₃²⁻, intensifying with potential from 1.22 to 1.62 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In 0.1 M KOH + 0.1 M CO₃²⁻, the peaks at 1500 cm⁻¹ and 1680 cm⁻¹ correspond to the C–O and C=O stretching vibrations of interfacial CO₃²⁻, respectively. They intensify gradually as the potential increases from 1.22 to 1.62 V vs. RHE.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR confirms intercalation with prominent C-O and C=O stretching vibrations in model catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR peaks corresponding to the C-O and C=O stretching vibrations are also prominent among the model catalysts after intercalation (Fig. S16).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co and Ni K-edge XANES show negative energy shift and increased white line intensity upon CO₃²⁻ intercalation, indicating reduced oxidation state and M-O covalency. EXAFS shows increased Co-O/Ni-O bond lengths.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of the Co and Ni K-edges... reveal a negative shift in the photon energy upon carbonate ion intercalation... The fitted Co-O/Ni-O and Co-Co/Ni-M bond lengths of all the model catalysts are summarized in Fig. 5e...

nodes.characterization_summary: Operando Raman of NiCoOOH shows Ni³⁺-O A₁g peak at 545 cm⁻¹ redshifts by 38 cm⁻¹ during ¹⁸O incorporation and blueshifts during release. NiCoOOH-2CO₃²⁻ shows suppressed LO release rate (0.80 cm⁻¹ min⁻¹ vs 1.40 cm⁻¹ min⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In NiOOH, the peaks at 486 and 545 cm⁻¹ correspond to E_g bending and A₁g stretching vibrations of Ni³⁺-O vibrations... the peaks of both the NiCoOOH and NiCoOOH-2CO₃²⁻ catalysts clearly redshift by 38 cm⁻¹ during the ¹⁸O incorporation step...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl measurements show ECSA of catalysts does not vary significantly during CL and CCL looping tests.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Notably, the current density in all LSVs is normalized to the electrochemical surface area (ECSA), which does not vary significantly during both looping tests, as shown by the double-layer capacitance (C_dl) in Fig. S3.

nodes.characterization_summary: Spent catalysts show relatively low leaching rate of transition metals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The inductively coupled plasma‒mass spectrometry (ICP‒MS) results in Fig. S38 show the relatively low leaching rate of transition metals from the catalysts to the electrolyte.
